title: Sylvester–Frobenius: g(m, n) = mn − m − n for Coprime m, n > 1

problemStatement.formal: \gcd(m,n)=1,\ m,n>1 \Rightarrow g(m,n) = mn - m - n,\ \text{the largest integer not of the form } am+bn,\ a,b \in \mathbb{N}.
problemStatement.plain: The two-coin Frobenius / 'Chicken McNugget' theorem: with coprime denominations $m, n > 1$, the largest amount that cannot be made as a nonnegative combination $am + bn$ is exactly $mn - m - n$. Every integer beyond it is representable. The classic $m=3, n=5$ gives $g = 7$. It is the one clean closed form of the coin problem (none exists for $\ge 3$ generators).

insights: Sylvester–Frobenius g(m,n)=mn-m-n for coprime m,n>1 is Mathlib's `frobeniusNumber_pair : FrobeniusNumber (m*n-m-n) {m,n}` where `FrobeniusNumber n s := IsGreatest {k | k ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure s} n` — a canonical predicate, NOT a function. The gallery parent `Proofs/FrobeniusNumber.lean` instead uses a homemade `Representable`/`frobeniusNumber` API; this entry's distinct value is restating the theorem on Mathlib's verified IsGreatest/closure footing.

`AddSubmonoid.mem_closure_pair (a b c) : c ∈ closure {a,b} ↔ ∃ m n:ℕ, m•a+n•b=c` is the elementary bridge; over ℕ `smul_eq_mul` turns it into `∃ a b, a*m+b*n=k`, so closure-membership reads as the elementary representability of the parent entry.

`frobeniusNumber_iff : FrobeniusNumber n s ↔ n ∉ closure s ∧ ∀ k>n, k ∈ closure s` cleanly splits the IsGreatest claim into the two halves of Sylvester's theorem (extremal value not representable; everything above representable).

`frobeniusNumber_pair` and `FrobeniusNumber`/`frobeniusNumber_iff` live at ROOT namespace (the `namespace Nat` block starts AFTER them in Mathlib/NumberTheory/FrobeniusNumber.lean), though `Coprime` in the signature is `Nat.Coprime`.

McNugget instance g(3,5)=7: rewrite `(7:ℕ)=3*5-3-5` by norm_num, then `frobeniusNumber_pair (by decide) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)`; `decide` (not native_decide) for `Nat.Coprime 3 5` keeps it 0-axiom (only propext/Choice/Quot.sound).
